guitar.notes: Craig Nicholls associated with Fender Jaguar/Mustang style garage gear, not strongly iconic.

tone.target: bright garage-punk crunch with fuzz edge
tone.profile: bright garage-punk crunch with fuzz edge
tone.summary: A tight signal chain starting with a Gate for noise control, followed by an OD boost for initial punch. The core tone uses the Fuzz distortion to provide the required edge, feeding into a UK 45 amp model paired with a bright UK Vintage 4x12 cabinet to capture the raw garage-punk sound.
corrections: keep fuzz as edge, not full Muff wall
favor raw crunch over thick saturation

rig.name: The Vines - Get Free - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain noise and hum inherent in punk/garage tones.
Provide initial aggressive punch and tighten the attack for rhythm playing.
blocks.gap: No dedicated pre-gain boost, using general Boost module.

blocks.purpose: Generate the required 'fuzz edge' and raw saturation without becoming a thick Muff wall.
Simulate the punchy, British combo sound (Plexi/Marshall style) needed for garage rock.
Provide the punchy, classic British cabinet sound matching the genre clues.
Sculpt the tone by boosting upper mids and trebles for maximum brightness and cutting through a mix.
Optional subtle modulation for texture, but kept off to avoid heavy modulation as requested.
Minimal delay for rhythmic definition without adding deep reverb or wash.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for a more aggressive, open-sounding 4x12 to better capture raw garage punk energy.

proposals.reason: Enhance raw, aggressive punch and open sound required for garage rock.
